correctness.rationale: For a selected vertex in part \(V_i\), the omitted neighbors are exactly \(C\setminus V_i\). Hence witnessing an omitted vertex \(u\) is equivalent to \(C\setminus V_i=\{u\}\). This identity proves the complete cases \(|C|=0\), \(|C|=1\), the exact two-vertex boundary, and impossibility for \(|C|\ge3\). Counting valid complements gives the stated enumerator. Exhaustive replay through order 10 checks 64,916 subsets across 128 part profiles and agrees with every coefficient, minimum, and special-case boundary.

originality.rationale: The 2013 founding source gives the definition and scalar clique, star, and complete-bipartite values. The Klein--Rodríguez-Velázquez--Yi full text explicitly gives the arbitrary complete-multipartite scalar formula, and the Ghanbari--Jäger--Lehtilä full text counts minimum sets for cliques, stars, and complete bipartite graphs. Those statements are strictly weaker than the retained all-set classification and full cardinality enumerator for arbitrary part sizes. Focused published-finding corpus and web searches found no matching arbitrary complete-multipartite all-set theorem. The complete-bipartite minimum-set count is explicitly treated as a prior-covered special case.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification of every feasible set for a standard graph class, not a narrow numerical slice. It strengthens a known arbitrary-part scalar formula and known clique/star/biclique minimum-set counts to a full arbitrary-part census, revealing that all feasible complements have size at most two and giving the exact cross-part coefficient.
